pageCache.text:
Good Schools Guide, 2024
An award-winning school
A top choice school for girls in south London
Sydenham & Dulwich Girls aims to inspire the future generations of creators, independent thinkers and trailblazers. We open eyes and hearts by educating the whole person: to balance mind, body and soul. Our diversity of academic and enrichment opportunities enables every girl to forge her own path, strive to be her best and excel. While no path is the same, each girl’s journey leads to valuable development and meaningful self-discovery. A proud member of the Girls’ Day School Trust (GDST) family of schools, we develop character beyond the curriculum.
Antonia Geldeard Head
We are delighted to have been commended in the Independent Girls’ School of the Year category at this year’s Independent Schools of the Year Awards!
Our focus on preparing girls for their futures goes beyond the traditional careers advice or life skills development, understanding that the world is evolving at a rapid rate, and our girls are likely to be entering careers that do not yet exist. As research shows that young women often feel underprepared for life beyond school, we have tackled this head on, offering a personalised, future-focused curriculum that equips every girl with the confidence, curiosity and clarity to own her future.
This recognition speaks directly to the curiosity, resilience and kindness we see from our girls every day, and to the dedication of those who support them on every step of their individual journey.
“There are so many skills you will gain just from being at Sydenham; being in an environment filled with incredible women who know how to speak up for themselves and others, who aren’t constrained by gender stereotypes about what they can be and knowing that they can do literally anything that they set their minds to. This spirit of Sydenham has carried me far.”
– Dr Sigourney Bonner, Class of 2009

pageCache.pageTitle: Head's Vision - Sydenham & Dulwich, South London
pageCache.text:
HEAD'S VISION
At Sydenham & Dulwich Girls, we believe that learning should be adventurous and fun. Joyful voices resound in our classrooms and corridors. This is a happy community – active and alive to the potential within each school day.
Our pioneering spirit, forged by our brave founders whose anglo-saxon motto, Nyle ye drede (fear nothing) underpins our ethos: forward thinking and curious, embracing experimentation and innovation.
This journey from the magic of our Reception classrooms to the sparky debate resonating from our Upper School spaces, encompasses three key pillars of thought to develop each individual as a whole person, well prepared for life in mind, body and soul.
Academic Expertise
Our education is designed in all areas to offer intellectual challenge and creative opportunity, championing purposeful, flexible young minds and growing confidence. Our expert teachers are engaged, skilful practitioners, lifelong learners and committed to impactful relationships with each child, understanding individual needs.
We believe that creativity and excellence flourishes when young girls are inspired, given the space to explore, and, importantly, feel that their individual achievements matter. Our curriculum is contemporary and relevant, with dynamic, independent learning opportunities. We embrace dialogue and debate, academic risk-taking and inquiry. We are fully engaged with new technologies, including harnessing the potential of AI, but not swayed by every fad.
Personal Development
We are all about whole personhood – building the strongest version of ourselves. Our community is unapologetically committed to empowering girls to build the skillset needed to navigate their world and their futures. We believe in the power of collective voices: a strong ‘we’ is notable at Sydenham & Dulwich Girls, borne out of achieving the right balance between individual confidence and a culture of care.
Our personal development programmes are bespoke – designed with wellbeing in mind and sensitive to each individual, age, context and environment. Our diverse, inclusive community is unique – girls embracing their differences, celebrating each other’s achievements, and rejecting perfectionist, stereotypical versions of themselves.
Future Ready
To be truly well prepared, our young girls have their eyes opened to their potential and their passions. It is our mission to inspire young women from an early age to recognise that they can forge their own path and aim high, supported by our team of experts. Our Futures Programme across the whole school is ambitious and determined for every child – looking outwards, drawing inspiration from our many successful alumnae, exploring the multi-faceted world of work and fostering important employability skills..
This specialised education, both at Junior and Senior, alongside the core curriculum, fosters intelligent thinkers, culturally and morally aware, as well as creative, problem solvers who collaborate within teams and articulate their thoughts with great passion alongside emotional understanding. Our young women, when they leave us, are successful leaders and role models, fully prepared.
The Sydenham & Dulwich Girls curriculum is deliberately designed to deliver academic excellence alongside a broad education in critical thinking, problem solving, visual culture, digital innovation and emotional intelligence.
What makes us special?
Girls at Sydenham & Dulwich are ambitious and open minded. They are also well rounded, intellectually curious, down to earth and happy.
Self-belief and happiness, alongside a ‘can do’ approach to every aspect of school life, enable our girls to thrive and succeed, and they leave us equipped with the skills and confidence to thrive in their future.
We believe our pupils deserve the highest standards of classroom practice, as well as exciting, challenging and enriching co-curricular opportunities, in an inspirational environment where they can be themselves and learn to be independent, resilient and confident.
The 2024 ISI report recognises the committed and passionate leadership group who drive the school forward, supported wholeheartedly by the staff, which leads to a positive and effective learning environment, benefitting pupils’ development as young people, ready for their futures. Leaders work together successfully with a clear focus on educating the whole person. They actively promote the wellbeing of all pupils, taking a strategic and inclusive approach.
Purpose & Strategy
To align with our future-ready vision and core values, our Purpose and Strategy 2026–2030 outlines our strategic roadmap for the years ahead. Supported by a detailed internal Action Plan, this document outlines our strategic roadmap for the school over the next coming years, setting a clear path for academic excellence, innovation, and pupil well-being.
Good Schools Guide Senior Review
“With an inspiring head at the helm, expert teaching and a warm, nurturing atmosphere, Sydenham High School is powering ahead at full steam. Academic results are on the up and these energetic, sparky girls are encouraged to be go-getting and ambitious right from the start.”
Good Schools Guide Junior Review
“A lovely school that offers myriad opportunities to these bright, buzzy girls. Parent after parent told us how happy their children are at the Prep. One said her family had been thinking of moving out of London but had decided against it because she couldn’t bear to move her daughters from a school where they are flourishing on every level.”
Visit us

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Values | Sydenham High School | GDST
pageCache.text:
OUR VALUES
We inspire the future generations of creators, independent thinkers and trailblazers, opening eyes and hearts by educating the whole person: to balance mind, body and soul. Our diversity of academic and enrichment opportunities enables every girl to forge her own path.
At Sydenham & Dulwich Girls we have a strong ethos of personalised education – we are here for ambitious, the creative, the courageous, the curious, the trailblazers and more!
Sydenham & Dulwich Girls is part of the Girls’ Day School Trust, the leading group of independent girls’ schools in the UK. Providing a first-class education for girls was the aim of our founders in 1887 and, though the outlook and opportunities for girls may have changed, our educational goals and ethos remain the same.
Our diversity of academic and enrichment opportunities enables every girl to forge her own path, strive to be her best and excel. Educating the whole person leads to happy, confident and courageous children who flourish and make a positive difference to their community.
What makes a Sydenham girl?
Curiosity for learning
Girls are empowered to learn without limits, cultivating an intellectual and creative mindset through a joyful learning.
Courage & character
We foster in every girl the strength of character and courage to discover and pursue her own path.
Culture of kindness
A happy and respectful community with strong relationships, prioritising every child’s wellbeing and celebrating diversity.
Generosity of spirit
Our girls are outward looking, giving back, taking on leadership and having a positive impact.
A sense of community pervades the whole school. Pupils respect and support each other wholeheartedly.
ISI, 2024
Living our values
Our core values, created by the school community, define what it means to be a Sydenham girl:
We aim to inspire future generations of creators, independent thinkers, and trailblazers by educating the whole person—balancing mind, body, and soul. Through a diverse range of academic and enrichment opportunities, every pupil is empowered to forge their own path.

Curiosity for Learning

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 5 explore Earth and Space at the Science Museum - Sydenham & Dulwich
pageCache.text:
Year 5 explore Earth and Space at the Science Museum
Bringing learning to life
Beginning in the Space Galleries, pupils learnt about important discoveries in space exploration and the contributions of many inspiring female scientists, sparking curiosity and helping bring learning to life!
Pupils also visited the IMAX Cinema to see a 3D rendition of A Beautiful Planet. The film was absolutely breathtaking, giving a powerful view of Earth from space and a unique experience of seeing the astronauts that live and work on the International Space Station. It was an unforgettable experience that left everyone in awe.
After lunch, girls explored the interactive Wonderlab, where they engaged with a wide range of hands-on activities linked to scientific concepts such as reflection, light, sound and friction. The exciting exhibits encouraged exploration, questioning and discovery, making science both fun and memorable!
It was a wonderful day filled with learning, excitement, and inspiration and the pupils represented the school brilliantly throughout the trip.

Year 5 & 6 Music Café
It was wonderful to see so many of our musicians perform so confidently, so early in the year! These informal performances give a wonderful insight into the girls’ musical development and individual journeys, and it is always a pleasure to see how they are progressing.
The Music Cafés are also a fantastic opportunity for the girls to practise performing in a supportive and encouraging environment, helping them to build confidence and become more comfortable sharing their music with others. Most importantly, it is lovely to see how much the girls support and encourage one another, celebrating each other’s achievements and creating such a warm and positive musical community.

pageCache.pageTitle: GDST Junior Mathematics Conference - Sydenham & Dulwich
pageCache.text:
GDST Junior Mathematics Conference
Magical Maths!
Year 6 pupils represented Sydenham & Dulwich Girls at the prestigious GDST Mathematics Conference, hosted at the Oxford University Mathematical Institute.
Under the theme ‘Magical Maths!’, pupils collaborated with peers from fellow GDST schools to complete rigorous mathematical investigations before taking part in a lively inter-school quiz. It was a full and rewarding day, and the girls returned full of excitement having engaged with mathematics in an exceptionally inspiring academic environment.
‘I really enjoyed learning the playing card magic tricks, you had to really think when trying to solve how they were done and I got to take part in the presentation and wear a cool hat!’ – Winnie
‘We worked hard as a team to use paper folding techniques to make a dodecahedron, it was great fun!’ – Minnie & Annabelle

pageCache.pageTitle: Charity & Partnerships | Sydenham & Dulwich Girls' GDST
pageCache.text:
CHARITY & PARTNERSHIPS
Our school value: Generosity of Spirit is all about giving back – we fundraise throughout the year and enjoy partnering with local schools and organisations.
Community partnerships and charitable activities are integral parts of school life at Sydenham High and pupils welcome the opportunity to give back in whatever way they can.
Sydenham High has a number of links and partnerships, both near and far. We are a patron of Sydenham Arts and we have collaborated on numerous projects to date, including providing venues for their events, such as the Artists Trail.
Year 12 students undertake community service and volunteering for the year as part of our bespoke Personal Development strand of our Sixth Form offer. Some girls choose to help out in their former primary schools, some serve in charity shops and some assist in hospitals and local hospices. We aim to engage with the local community wherever possible, including collecting for the Lewisham Food Bank and we regularly host community groups and courses within the school. In Year 10 the girls take part in local community service, coming up with their own project ideas to support local services and amenities. We often run events for local maintained schools and the school has recently established a partnership with a local primary school in Forest Hill.
Primary School Collaborations
All students in year 12 undertake a volunteering placement in the Spring Term. We have established partnerships with Holy Trinity and St Bartholomew’s Primary Schools.
Our Head of Languages runs French lessons at Holy Trinity Primary, with new Art and Reading clubs beginning.
Invitations to workshops and performances.
Use of theatre and facilities for end of year school productions and to sit LAMDA exams.
Use of sports ground and the astroturf for primary school sports days and Lewisham sporting tournaments.
Sixth formers reading to Prep School pupils.
Debating and other academic collaborative activities with Dulwich College Junior School.
Secondary School Collaborations
International School link with Kyoto Seibo Gakuin Girls’ School.
Host Academic Electives with Dulwich College and JAGS, including Anatomical Studies, and Debunking Medical Myths: from stem cells to superheroes.
One Voice collaboration with Dulwich Prep & Senior
FarmEd in Oxfordshire: building on our commitment to educating about sustainability.
Futures Fairs and other events, such as the GCSE Accelerator Programme.
#700STEMChallenge essay writing competition.
Subject Masterclasses.
Teaching at Saturday School for local primaries with Dulwich College.
Lewisham Librarians meeting of 7 local schools held at SHS sharing best practice and selecting shortlist for Lewisham Book Awards.
Participation in GDST GCSE Astronomy and Space Tech programmes, as well as hosting GDST LEAD South.
Local community links
Westwood House Care Home and Pear Tree Care Home volunteering.
Volunteering and musical collaboration with the local ageing well community at Grove Centre Church, Sydenham
Phab Clubs for local disabled children: our pupils play games, do mindful activities and befriend.
Young Mayor of Lewisham initiative: increased pupil participation, including standing as candidates.
Sydenham Arts: patronage to support this local charity and some workshops and opportunities for pupils offered.
Prep Flourish and Fundraise Committee pupils raised money for, and donated artwork to, local Sydenham Community Gardens, supporting local community members with dementia.
Charitable activities
Fundraising is a huge part of our culture, with the girls choosing charities for each House and organising multiple events per year.
Generosity of Spirit is one of the core values of Sydenham High. Throughout the years, we have been dedicated to working with various charities, both locally and nationally, to support their worthy causes. We aim to elevate our efforts by harnessing our powerful house spirit to enhance our charity work, allowing each house to select a charity they would like to support throughout the year.
Stanley House: St Christopher’s
Our local St Christopher’s Hospice is only a few roads away, and close to our hearts, offering world class palliative and end of life care to everyone who needs it, whenever or wherever that may be. Founded by Dame Cicely founded in 1967 as the first hospice linking expert pain and symptom control, compassionate care, teaching and clinical research, St Christopher’s has been a pioneer in the field of palliative medicine, which is now established worldwide.
Shirreff House: Freedom4Girls
Freedom4Girls is a charity dedicated to fighting period poverty and promoting menstrual health. Founded to address the stigma and barriers surrounding menstruation, Freedom4Girls provides essential menstrual products and educational workshops, ensuring that no girl misses school or a woman misses work due to her period.
Gurney House: St Mungo’s
St Mungo’s is a charity dedicated to ending homelessness and helping people rebuild their lives. It provides vital services, including outreach support, accommodation, and healthcare, helping individuals recover from homelessness and reintegrate into society.
Grey House: Lives Not Knives
Lives Not Knives is committed to preventing youth violence and empowering young people through education and support. The charity offers mentoring, workshops, and opportunities for young people to engage in community projects that promote safety and wellbeing.
Recent fundraising
After a full week of end-of-year assessments, our Year 7 pupils swapped exam halls for fresh air as they headed to Crystal Palace Park for their House Charity Walk. With the sun shining, it was the perfect way to unwind, reconnect with friends, and raise funds for a meaningful cause.
Sponsored per lap, the walk soon turned into a joyful competition, with many pupils racing each other to complete as many laps as possible. Spirits were high as the year group demonstrated fantastic energy, teamwork and generosity – all while enjoying the great outdoors.
And of course, no summer walk would be complete without a sweet treat! The ice cream van proved extremely popular, with pupils (and staff!) forming a well-deserved queue for their cheerful reward.
A big thank you to everyone who sponsored and supported the event. We are incredibly proud of our Year 7s for their enthusiasm, kindness and House spirit – a wonderful reflection of Sydenham High’s values!
Sydenham High was buzzing with excitement as Year 8 hosted their House Charity Events, raising a fantastic £359.47 for their House charities. After weeks of planning, pupils came together to deliver a brilliant range of fundraising activities, strengthening their House spirit while supporting meaningful causes.
Grey raised £91.55 for Lives Not Knives with a biscuit decorating stall. Shirreff brought in £68.65 for Freedom4Girls with a nail salon and bath bomb sales. Stanley’s Cosy Day, featuring Oodies, Onesies, and hot chocolate, raised £151 for St Christopher’s Hospice. Gurney’s ‘Guess the Sweets’ challenge raised £49.27 for St Mungo’s.
The energy, teamwork, and generosity shown by Year 8 were truly inspiring.
Year 9 took the lead on house fundraising for their respective charities, bringing an incredible range of creative ideas to life! The action-packed Grey’s Red Light/Green Light game had everyone involved, while Gurney’s mystery bag draw offered a chance to try their luck. Stanley’s “Guess the Staff Baby Photo” was truly mind-blowing, and Shirreff’s car and minibus cleaning service added a wonderful act of service element to the day.
The event was buzzing with energy, offering something for everyone to enjoy. Year 9 worked together seamlessly, and their efforts paid off, raising an impressive total of £215, with Shirreff raising £110, Grey £33, Gurney £44, and Stanley £28 for their chosen causes. A big congratulations to them for their hard work, and thank you to all the pupils and staff who took part in making the day a massive success!
The end of term culminated with another charity event, this time soaking the teachers with wet sponges – or trying to! Year 10’s charity event was a great success.
Grey House kicked off its first House fundraising event today for Lives Not Knives, with an exciting, themed fashion show organised and run by our Year 11 Grey House Charity leaders. The atmosphere was filled with energy as everyone came together to support a great cause. The participants took the stage with confidence and joy, showing off their unique styles, while their friends cheered them on. It was a fantastic turnout for an even better cause.
Tell us your fundraising ideas

pageCache.pageTitle: Junior Futures Programme South London | Sydenham & Dulwich Girls GDST
pageCache.text:
DAYDREAM BELIEVERS
Our Futures Programme begins in our Junior School, where curiosity is sparked and imagination ignited.
Our pioneering ‘Daydream Believers’ is a bespoke programme that sets us apart, fostering future-forward thinkers with a unique blend of academic sparkle and character development. Pupils engage in real-world problem-solving, from sustainability challenges to augmented reality-driven projects, working alongside industry leaders. This initiative nurtures critical thinking, collaboration, and adaptability—key future skills. Pupil engagement, external awards, and feedback from secondary schools further confirm our impact.
Our innovative, forward-thinking approach is not just shaping academic achievers but empowering young changemakers who are ready to lead with passion and purpose. We know that every child has a spark of creativity waiting to be kindled, and we make space for it to ignite. Sydenham & Dulwich Girls’ Junior School is a beacon of excellence in independent education, proving that when innovation meets care, the possibilities for our Giraffe Girls are limitless.
Our initiative is why we were Shortlisted for Prep School of the Year 2025 at the Independent Schools of the Year Awards!
Ambitious Giraffe Girls
We believe in creating fearless, future-ready learners who are both academically ambitious and emotionally intelligent. We combine cutting-edge education with a strong pastoral foundation to empower girls as innovators, leaders, and change-makers. Education here is not just about knowledge acquisition but about developing confident, adaptable individuals who can thrive in an evolving world. Our pupils actively engage in shaping their own futures, making learning deeply personal and inspiring. At the heart of this initiative is our Giraffe Girl ethos, where every pupil is encouraged to aim high, stand tall and proud, and stick their neck out to help others.
Leadership
We redefine what it means to educate the next generation of fearless, future-forward thinkers. Through our innovative duality approach, to developing the whole child within our ‘Daydream Believers’ initiative, an ambitious learning culture, and our expert, evidence-informed pastoral care, we empower our pupils to become confident, compassionate leaders.
Discover the magic

pageCache.pageTitle: Junior Sports Report: 2 October 2026 - Sydenham & Dulwich
pageCache.text:
Junior Sports Report: 2 October 2026
U11 Football vs Rosemead
On Monday afternoon, our U11 footballers travelled to Rosemead for an engaging set of fixtures.
It was fantastic to see several players representing the school for the very first time in football, joining our 15-player squad which was divided into two balanced, mixed-ability teams. This gave every girl valuable match time and an opportunity to develop her game across a pair of competitive 20-minute matches against Rosemead’s A team.
Our first team played out an entertaining 0-0 draw in a tight contest. Defence was the highlight of the match, anchored by two fantastic goalkeeping performances: Florence commanded her box brilliantly in the first half with sharp communication and decisive rushing off her line, whilst Georgie pulled off a series of brilliant saves in the second half. Although the outfield players constructed some bright attacking moves, they just couldn’t find the decisive touch. Cece was deservedly awarded Opposition Player of the Match for her tireless energy and box-to-box presence from central midfield.
Our second team faced a tough battle, ultimately falling to a 3-0 defeat, but the scoreline didn’t reflect the quality of their performance. In fact, they played some of our best football of the afternoon, particularly in a vibrant second half where Sadie and Zina created numerous goalscoring opportunities with their direct, energetic runs. Maya earned Opposition Player of the Match honours for a magnificent display in central midfield, working relentlessly to connect defence and attack throughout.
Well done to all the girls involved for showing great teamwork, spirit, and sportsmanship throughout the afternoon!
U9 Netball vs Streatham & Clapham High School
Year 4 had an exciting start to their netball season in their very first fixture representing Sydenham & Dulwich Girls and against Streatham & Clapham High School. For the girls, this was a thrilling new experience, and every player worked remarkably hard while learning a great deal on the court.
Across all three teams, the players demonstrated fantastic resilience, communicated effectively and listened closely to coaching feedback as the games progressed. It was a closely fought contest from start to finish, with the overall result narrowly decided by just a single goal.
A special mention goes to Saskia, who excelled in attack by consistently finding strong positions in the circle to shoot. Individual Players of the Match were also celebrated across each team: Taylor was named Player of the Match for the Yellow team for her tight marking and constant pressure on her opponent; Marnie earned the honor for the Green team thanks to her fantastic reading of the game and repeated interceptions; and Alivia took Player of the Match for the Blue team with her quick dodging and energetic drives into space. It was a wonderful first outing for Year 4, full of teamwork, progress, and brilliant sportsmanship.
U11 Netball vs Bromley High School
It was a brilliant week of netball for our U11 squads, with so many pupils having the opportunity to take to the court in an afternoon filled with enthusiasm, teamwork, and great sportsmanship against Bromley High School.
The A Team fought hard in an incredibly close and competitive match, narrowly missing out on a win with a tight 6–4 scoreline. The players displayed fantastic resilience throughout, with Ella earning Player of the Match at Goal Shooter for her composure and relentless work rate.
The B Team put on a sensational performance, securing a brilliant 16–1 victory. The squad showed superb versatility, with players adapting seamlessly across different positions. Player of the Match went to Maya M for her outstanding shooting consistency.
In another well-contested fixture, the C Team earned a fantastic 4–2 win thanks to sharp court movement and disciplined play. Evie S was named Player of the Match for her impressive tracking and strong, decisive passing.
Rounding off a wonderful afternoon, the D Team delivered a great performance to take a deserved 3–1 victory. Olivia was awarded Player of the Match for consistently finding great space and distributing the ball with brilliant accuracy.
A huge well done to every single pupil who represented the school this week—your hard work, enthusiasm, and team spirit made everyone very proud!

Our Year 1 girls enjoyed a truly magical visit to the ArtPlay Pavilion at Dulwich Picture Gallery, and what a resounding success it was! Filled with laughter, curious exploration, and hands on discovery, the trip provided an unforgettable blending of art and creative play.
Designed specifically as an immersive sensory experience for young minds, the ArtPlay Pavilion brings classic masterpieces to life in the most enchanting ways. The girls stepped into a world where art is not just something you look at on a wall, but something you can touch, move through, and experience with all your senses.
The joy and enthusiasm were contagious, with the girls fully engaged from start to finish!

pageCache.pageTitle: Personal Development | Sydenham & Dulwich Girls | GDST
pageCache.text:
PERSONAL DEVELOPMENT
Education is not just about curriculum content, it shapes you as a person, and we are committed to ensuring that all our girls know themselves and build core skills for a successful life.
Academic study lies at the heart of Sixth Form life but there is a huge amount on offer beyond this. It is the balance of the co-curricular enrichment that makes Sydenham High School such an inspiring place to grow during your Sixth Form years. There are greater responsibilities on offer, as well as freedoms to develop self-motivation and independence.
When you start in Year 12 there is a bespoke induction programme to aid the transition to Sixth Form including welcome events, team building activities, and personalised curriculum meetings.
There are a wide range of educational visits on offer as part of the curriculum. In previous years our students have visited New York, and our sister school in Nepal, a school that we helped to rebuild after the earthquake in 2015, alongside the charity In Your Hands.
The Elevate Curriculum
Ten years ago, our Power Skills Programme was created as a flagship careers initiative, totally unique to Sydenham & Dulwich Girls. As Reuters reported, “power skills aren’t just nice to have— they are essential skills for an ever-changing workplace.” Developing students in terms of their communication, emotional intelligence and interpersonal skills are at the forefront of the programme and allow students to be confident in navigating the world of work.
The Elevate Curriculum launched in 2025, equipping students with relevant and transferable skills for life beyond school:
o Developing emotional intelligence o Strong oracy: interview, communication and presentational skills o Strategic outlooks: positive, personal branding and the professional marketplace o Building digital literacy further – AI for innovation o Exploring the benefits of mentoring and successful networking skills o Knowing your rights within the workplace for an inclusive environment o Volunteering and community impact
Leadership & Skills
The Young Leadership Team play an important role in the school. The leadership skills gained from these roles are invaluable, and give you the opportunity to engage with the rest of the school community.
Sixth formers are actively encouraged to get involved with some of the many other activities that are on offer, including:
– GDST Leadership & Enterprise Advanced Diploma – Dulwich College Saturday School – Gold Duke of Edinburgh’s Award – School societies such as Literary Society, AfroCaribbean Society and BioChemMedSoc
Partnerships & Volunteering
Volunteering within the local community is an opportunity to give back to the people and area around you, whilst also developing key skills in communication, empathy and teamwork. There are range on offer from supporting in local primary schools, working in residential homes or undertaking community project work.
A number of Sixth Formers are trained to teach at the Dulwich College Saturday school where gifted and talented pupils from local primary schools are given extra tuition, particularly in maths, literacy and science. Others choose to volunteer at local charity shops, or give their time supporting the Junior School by running clubs or getting involved with local primary schools.
Wellbeing
Mental health and wellbeing are as important as physical health. We offer outstanding Pastoral care and guidance to bring out the very best in you. Our friendly, mutually supportive and aspirational environment values each girl as an individual. Sixth Formers have specific pastoral needs and we provide comprehensive and practical pastoral support that enables you to navigate successfully the potential pressures you might encounter.
The impactful relationships between staff and girls ensures tailored support, and our pioneering, innovative PSHE programme helps navigate real-world issues young people are facing today.
The strong community feel of our Sixth Form, alongside robust systems of monitoring and reporting, ensures Sixth Form is rewarding, successful and positive.
Explore your future

pageCache.pageTitle: Academic Expertise | Sydenham & Dulwich Girls | GDST
pageCache.text:
ACADEMIC EXPERTISE
We pride ourselves on our academic success within the Sixth Form. Our girls aim high and achieve excellent results. The wide range of subject choices, taught by dedicated subject specialists, ensures that we support your interests and your potential career path.
We offer a fantastic range of 28 subject choices, taught by dedicated subject specialists, ensures that we support your interests and your potential career path. You will experience a greater freedom and enjoy studying subjects that genuinely interest you, in smaller classes, while forming more mature relationships with your teachers who will support you every step of the way.
We aren’t just focused on academic success. We also want you to learn how to think, to be inquisitive so that we set you up for a lifetime of thinking critically to help your future career path. Seminar style lessons and independent learning not only help prepare you for university, but also create motivated learners.
Academic pathways
We offer a broad range of subjects at Sydenham & Dulwich Girls and students choose one of the pathways below:
Pathway 1: Three A Levels + Extended Project Qualification Pathway 2: Four A Levels Pathway 3: Four A Levels + Extended Project Qualification
Our Sixth Form offering is separated into three strands: Personal Development, Academic Expertise and Future Pathways.
A Levels allow students to focus on the subjects they wish to understand in greater depth. Smaller class sizes allow for more seminar style learning which challenges student understanding, alongside providing a platform for more independent study. Other qualifications also count toward UCAS points such as Grade 8 Music or a LAMDA discipline, a gold Duke of Edinburgh’s Award as well as the gold Crest Science Award.
The EPQ
The Extended Project Qualification (EPQ) is a Level 3 stand alone academic qualification, equating to half an A Level. It is an independent research project, guided by an experienced supervisor, and enables students to develop skills in the areas of problem-solving, critical thinking, analysis, synthesis evaluation and public speaking. Highly regarded by both universities and employers, many Russell Group universities take the EPQ into account as part of their holistic assessment of a student’s UCAS application.
Recent topics include: the Ebola outbreak, individual privacy legislation and the impact of Nazi Germany on the Bauhaus School. The independent research can be submitted in the form of an academic report of 5000 words or an artefact or product alongside a 2000 word essay. All students finish their EPQ by giving a 15 minute presentation followed by a question and answer session.
Students who do the EPQ also find that the skills are transferable to their other subjects and recent research has shown that students who complete the EPQ enhance their chances of achieving an A*-B in their other A Levels by 29%.
Year 12
Advanced Electives
Developing interests outside of the A Level curriculum is vital in helping to shape curious young people. Our enrichment programme offers a variety of courses that allow you to learn new skills or try an activity that challenges you physically or mentally. There is a wealth of courses available to you including political awareness, photography, first aid, rock climbing and sign language to name a few.
We operate an Advanced Electives Series in partnership with Dulwich College and JAGS. Electives run at Dulwich College and Sydenham & Dulwich Girls and there are a plethora of options to choose from such as Anatomical Studies, Debunking medical myths: from stem cells to superheros and Architectural History.
Dulwich College student

AWARDS & RECOGNITION
At Sydenham & Dulwich Girls we have a strong ethos of personalised education – we are here for ambitious, the creative, the courageous, the curious, the trailblazers and more! We remain ambitious and progressive, andwe are preparing each sparky girl not just for the next stage of her education but for the rest of her life.
We are proud to have had some exceptional comments from the Independent Schools Inspectorate, the Good Schools Guide, Talk Education and more, as well as being recognised for our excellent education at several awards over the years.
A future-focussed education

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Wellbeing Junior School London | Sydenham & Dulwich Girls
pageCache.text:
CARE & WELLBEING
The wellbeing of our pupils is paramount. Pastoral care is the cornerstone of our provision and we strive to ensure that each and every pupil is supported to feel happy, safe and secure within our school community.
Our approach to pastoral care at our Junior School focuses upon strong and positive relationships between pupils and staff as well as an open partnership with parents.
We also have clear expectations of behaviour enshrined in our Golden Rules:
There is strong pastoral support from teaching staff who closely monitor pupils’ progress, both socially and emotionally, throughout the year. The size of the school also makes a difference: pupils are visible and well-known as individuals. Staff can be flexible and responsive to the specific needs of every pupil as a unique individual.
Sydenham & Dulwich Girls’ Junior School has devised a Culture Curriculum, praised by ISI, to ensure exemplary behaviour for character development and attitudes to learning.
ISI, 2024
What is a Giraffe Girl?
Fina the giraffe is our Junior School mascot and our pupils are affectionately known as ‘Giraffe Girls’. They are kind, thoughtful, considerate, courageous, determined and diligent.
Our school thrives on supportive and warm relationships, with our Giraffe Girls standing tall, aiming high and sticking their necks out for other people.
Our hand drawn Giraffe Girl characters reflect our values. Are you an Ambitious Arya or a Kind Kalifa – perhaps a Networked Nelia?
We promote the qualities of our Giraffe Girl characters through themed weeks. Pupils may resonate with particular characters, but they are reminded that each and every quality is valued and form the foundation for a rounded member of society.
Play Leaders
Our older pupils are trained as Inspired Leaders, to organise and lead games and activities during playtime. They act as positive role models, promote social interaction, and help create a fun and engaging atmosphere on the playground.
The Wellbeing Hub
We are delighted to announce that we’ve invested in The Wellbeing Hub.
Supporting the mental health and wellbeing of our students, parents, and staff is a top priority for us.
Discover the magic

pageCache.pageTitle: Award-Winning Pastoral Care | Sydenham & Dulwich Girls GDST
pageCache.text:
CARE & WELLBEING
Our award-winning pastoral care puts every girl at the centre of their educational journey and the growth in their own personal development. They leave us grounded, rounded and above all happy.
Outstanding pastoral care has always been a feature of Sydenham & Dulwich Girls. Wellbeing it is intrinsically embedded throughout the school as a whole, firmly rooted into our ethos and the teaching offered by our dedicated staff. We believe in the importance of every girl learning to be respectful of themselves as well as others and encourage each pupil to focus on what makes them unique, treating everyone as an individual and supporting them through their journey. In September 2026 our new health and wellness space, Wellspring, will open. This area will house a gym as well as dance/ fitness studio on the ground floor and wellbeing and counsellor spaces above.
The wellbeing of all our pupils is a priority and we believe firmly in helping our pupils stay healthy and well, both in mind and body. The triangulation between pupil, school and home is paramount, and we encourage strong and supportive connections.
Inclusive SEN Provision 2025
Embedding EDI in the curriculum
Pastoral Care Champion
Student Wellbeing & Prep School of the Year
Reaching out for support
First point of content: Form Tutor
Other pastoral leads:
Head of Year 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and Sixth Form
Head of Lower School, Head of Upper School
The Deputy Head Pastoral has overall responsibility for the welfare of all the pupils in the school, as well as being the designated Senior Lead for Safeguarding and Child Protection.
Pupil Voice
We want our pupils to feel that they are being listened to. Everyone knows whom to approach should they need a listening ear or additional support. In addition, regular round table meetings enable pupils to express their views and present new ideas and initiatives.
Stepping up to Year 7
The programme is designed to scaffold pupils first few weeks of senior school and to acclimatise to new routines, expectations and relationships, promoting confidence and communication skills. Part of this initiative includes the opportunity to simply play at lunchtime. This is supervised by Head of Lower School, Head of Year 7 and is facilitated by the Young Leadership Team in Sixth Form.
Leadership opportunities
There are plenty of opportunities for pupils to take on responsibilities or develop leadership skills, through co-curricular pursuits or through the form group. Our House system also adds an additional layer of opportunity, as well as crucial integration with other year groups and forms, all of which helps prepare pupils for taking on larger roles in the wider life of the school community as they become older.
Engineer your future

pageCache.pageTitle: Head, Staff & Governors | Sydenham & Dulwich Girls' GDST
pageCache.text:
STAFF & GOVERNORS
Our school’s strategic vision is led by our experienced Senior Leadership Team, supported by a dedicated staff body across Junior, Senior and Sixth Form.
Senior Leadership Team
Antonia read English Literature at Trinity College, Cambridge University, graduating with an MA, and later a PGCE in English and Drama. After early years spent working as a television journalist, in factual programmes, she joined Alleyn’s School, in Dulwich, as an English and Drama teacher and was quickly promoted to a range of roles including Housemaster and Head of English. In 2017, Antonia moved to Trinity School, Croydon, to take up the role of Head of Sixth Form, overseeing academic and pastoral care, and in 2019 she was promoted to Deputy Head.
Antonia is passionate about educating bright and ambitious women of the future and has been Head of Sydenham & Dulwich Girls since September 2022, where girls are inspired to be creators, independent thinkers and trailblazers, empowered to discover and nurture their unique talents and forge their own future. With 25 years of experience in high achieving co-educational and single-sex schools, alongside parenting two teenagers in South London, Antonia brings invaluable insight into the London schools’ market. She has a wealth of experience in academic and pastoral matters, holding responsibilities over the course of her career in Sixth Form, enrichment, EPQ, school admissions and marketing, university admissions and careers as well as holding the position of Deputy Safeguarding Lead for many years. She also has experience as a primary school governor.
Following her high school education in Texas, Sarah graduated from Southern Methodist University (SMU) in Dallas with a degree in English and a minor in Political Science. During her undergraduate studies, she spent a formative year at the University of St Andrews, where she studied English and International Relations. Sarah began her career in the United States by joining Teach For America programme, teaching in the Baltimore City Public School system while simultaneously earning her MA in Teaching from Johns Hopkins University.
Upon moving to London with Teach First, Sarah continued to develop a broad, international understanding of educational systems. During her tenure as Assistant Head at St Dunstan’s College, Sarah led on the strategic development of SEND provision and the refinement of data systems, ensuring that academic tracking and inclusive practice translated into meaningful support for every pupil.
Now in her third girls’ school, Sarah is a firm believer in the unique power of an all-girls environment. She is inspired by the way Sydenham & Dulwich Girls pairs a strong sense of community with fearless academic ambition. As Deputy Head Academic, she is dedicated to ensuring that every student is empowered to achieve her very best, regardless of her starting point. Sarah is passionate about using research-informed practice to unlock potential, ensuring that every girl flourishes and leaves Sydenham with the confidence to forge her own future.
Educated at King Edward VI High School in Birmingham, Elyse went on to study Genetics with French at the University of Liverpool, spending a year at University in Poitiers gaining a Maitrise in Biochime whilst there. Elyse went on to achieve a PhD in Cancer Studies from the University of Birmingham, specialising in transcriptional regulation of viruses in cancer cells. Feeling that there was still yet more studying to be done, she then came to London to complete her PGCE at King’s College London. Elyse then spent eight years at Wimbledon High School GDST where she completed her science teacher training and quickly progressed to Head of Year and Head of PSHE while also having her first two daughters.
Elyse took up the role of Head of Biology at Sydenham & Dulwich Girls in 2015 and progressed to Director of Teaching and Learning 3 years later, having had her third (and final) daughter. Elyse took on the role of Deputy Head Pastoral just before the first COVID lockdown in 2020.
Rebecca graduated from the University of Southampton with a BA (Hons) in History before beginning her career in the technology sector, where she managed large-scale corporate hardware and software solutions. Her passion for education led her back to study, completing a PGCE in Secondary Education. She began her teaching career at Ashcroft Technology Academy as a History teacher, where she played a key role in introducing the International Baccalaureate (IB) programme to the Sixth Form and served as a mentor for trainee teachers. Rebecca then joined Harris Academy South Norwood as Head of History, later becoming Sixth Form Coordinator. In addition to her school-based roles, she held federation-wide responsibilities, including History Consultant – leading the development and standardisation of the Key Stage 3 History curriculum – and Federation Examination Supervisor for A Level History. With a strong foundation in both curriculum leadership and Sixth Form education, Rebecca was appointed Assistant Head at Sydenham & Dulwich Girls, where she began as Head of Sixth Form, drawing on her broad experience to support students’ academic and personal development, before moving into Deputy Head Staff & Operations in September 2026.
Lorna Dodds graduated from The University of Nottingham with a First-class BA honours degree in English Literature and German. She continued to nurture her love of books in a range of editorial roles in Publishing, as well as working in the Literary department of the WME talent agency. Realising that she is most inspired by the words and ideas of young minds, Lorna retrained to become an English teacher, earning her stripes in a range of inner-city London comprehensive schools, before becoming Head of A Level English, Head of Year 7 and then Assistant Director of Teaching and Learning at a London girls’ grammar school. Lorna joined the Senior Leadership Team at Sydenham & Dulwich Girls in 2021 as Assistant Head: Enrichment & Partnerships, and became Head of Sixth Form in 2026.
Zoe graduated from Cambridge University in 2003 with a First-Class Honours degree in Mathematics with Education. She has since enjoyed a rich and varied career as an excellent teacher across a wide range of settings including primary schools, special educational needs provision and secondary schools. Zoe led Mathematics at Notting Hill Prep School and also worked as a specialist Mathematics teacher at Sydenham & Dulwich Girls, where she inspired a love of the subject through her engaging teaching and strong relationships with pupils.
In her leadership roles, Zoe has been committed to building meaningful partnerships between staff, pupils and parents to ensure every child feels supported to thrive. Appointed Assistant Head Pupil Development and Enrichment in 2022, she enhanced the school’s clubs provision, House system and rewards structure. In 2023, she was promoted to Deputy Head Pastoral, reflecting her deep commitment to the wellbeing of every pupil, recognising it as central to academic and personal success.
Zoe is passionate about the power of girls’ education to give young women the confidence to be bold, brave and ambitious. She brings warmth, experience and vision to her role, championing opportunities for girls to grow as individuals, discover their voices and shape their own future.
Jane graduated with a Bachelor of Education, specialising in Science and Mathematics, from the University of Hertfordshire. With a career spanning 24 years as an outstanding practitioner across maintained, independent and international schools, she has led curriculum design and Mathematics development both at school and trust level. Jane’s leadership experience includes serving as Senior Leader at a large maintained primary school before moving to the British International School of Chicago – Lincoln Park, where she was Assistant Head Academic.
In 2022, Jane joined Sydenham High School as Assistant Head Teaching and Learning and, in recognition of her expertise and impact, was promoted to Deputy Head Academic in 2024. Alongside her school leadership roles, Jane has worked extensively with the National Centre for Excellence in the Teaching of Mathematics (NCETM), training as both a Primary Mastery Specialist and Professional Development Lead. She has led teacher research groups, contributed to the Department for Education’s China–England exchange, and worked as an international Mathematics consultant.
Jane is passionate about academic excellence underpinned by research and thoughtful pedagogy. She is committed to building confidence in learners through secure foundations, enabling all pupils to be stretched, challenged and inspired to achieve their very best. At Sydenham High, she believes in the importance of education that adds value to every child, whatever their starting point, ensuring that each pupil flourishes and fulfils her potential.
After attending Reigate Grammar School, Adam studied Modern History and Politics at Nottingham Trent University. He then completed officer training at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst and was commissioned into the Princess of Wales’s Royal Regiment. Adam saw active service in Northern Ireland and the Balkans and left the Army after ten years to start a new career in Finance. He worked for two large international banks in both corporate and wealth management roles and then, looking to return to a leadership and management role, moved to the City of London Corporation. Adam firstly oversaw the operational management of the Mansion House, the Lord Mayor of London’s official residence, and then moved location to become Director of Operations at the Central Criminal Court – the Old Bailey as it is more widely known. After fourteen years with the Corporation, Adam made the move into education joining Sydenham & Dulwich Girls as Director of Finance & Operations.
Governors & Trustees
Having attended Sydenham High School between 1998 and 2005, Zara Berry has most recently worked at Chatham House, The Royal Institute of International Affairs for over 12 years. In her position as Head of Individual Membership, she is part of the institute’s External Relations, Fundraising team, which is responsible for stakeholder engagement, relationship building and raising discretionary income critical to Chatham House fulfilling its mission. Chatham House, a world-leading policy institute, strives to help governments and societies build a sustainably secure, prosperous and just world.
Jacynth Bassett is the award-winning Founder and CEO of The Bias Cut – the first age-inclusive online fashion shopping platform – and global movement / community Ageism Is Never In Style®.
Having attended Sydenham High from aged 4 to aged 18, graduating in 2010, Jacynth went on to study Law at the University of Cambridge, where she became President of the Cambridge Law Society. Upon graduating, she decided to pivot away from law, and launched The Bias Cut in 2016 with the aim to pioneer age inclusivity in fashion, and address the gendered-ageism that females face throughout their entire life. Today, alongside The Bias Cut, Jacynth is a leading and highly sought-after pioneer and voice in the anti-ageism & age-inclusive fashion movement. She is regularly invited to aid and consult charities, research projects, educational establishments, organisations and businesses that are aiming to tackle ageism and create a more age-inclusive society.
RIBA, ARB, PGDipArch, BArch
Emily is an architect, currently an Associate at Apt. Emily’s work spans across private residential, housing schemes, hospitality and complex mixed-use developments working with clients across the private and public sectors. Her core drive is to create spaces and places grounded in their context, that benefit the wellbeing of the community and compliment the unique needs of the area. Emily has lived in Sydenham for the last 10 years, and is a mum to two children, Lucas (5) and Matilda (2).
MPhys (Oxford) Physics, MSc (London) Actuarial Finance, Fellow of the Institute of Actuaries, Investment Director
Cyprian is a qualified Actuary with focus on providing investment strategy advice to pension schemes, charities, endowments and other institutional clients. He is currently an Investment Director within an Asset Management firm in the City of London. He’s passionate about personal finance and the importance of financial education to students.
Ben has been a Civil Servant for nearly 25 years working in several Departments and in a range of roles including Policy, Operational Delivery and Programme Management. He is currently Programme Director for two major Government Programmes. He studied Politics, Philosophy and Economics with the Open University while working, graduating in 2013. Ben has a daughter in Sydenham High Prep and so has been involved in the school as a parent since 2020.
Suzanne is a Solicitor (LLB Exeter University); former partner at City solicitors Wedlake Bell London now semi-retired and working as a consultant to the firm. She joined the firm in 1979 and over the years she has done many management jobs including serving on various management committees, including trainee recruitment and the firm’s Board. She founded and headed the construction team which became and still is a very successful team. She was a member of various industry bodies and served for many years on the Technology and Construction Solicitors Association as a committee member.
Suzanne’s daughter was a pupil at Sydenham High School between 1998 and 2005 and is now a palliative care doctor. She is very grateful to the school for having nurtured her from when she arrived at the school lacking confidence, particularly academically: “She thrived and has not only been able to pursue the career she always wanted but also made life- long friends with whom she is still regularly in touch.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Diversity & Inclusion | Sydenham & Dulwich Girls GDST
pageCache.text:
DIVERSITY & INCLUSION
We are rightly proud of our reputation as an inclusive school, where girls know and understand themselves and others. A sense of belonging permeates our community.
ISI, 2024
We are proud of the inclusive nature of our school. Focusing on tolerance and respect for yourself and others is a cornerstone of our ethos. We believe in the importance of hearing, and acting upon, the voices within our community and ask for regular feedback and suggestions on how to improve our school. We understand that not all differences are visible and aim to ensure that a sense of belonging is instilled throughout our community.
Undivided is our annual programme of whole-school initiatives which celebrate a broad range of events throughout the year which are reflective of the diverse community that is Sydenham & Dulwich Girls. Our Undivided Lead coordinates activities and training throughout the year, and our pupils speak out to drive social change, with one of our alumnae setting up the Halo Code. ISI also noted: Pupils “firmly reject discrimination of any kind on any grounds”.
Culture & Identity Day
Every autumn, our Diversity & Inclusion Prefects run a day for everyone to showcase their heritage, culminating in a very popular ‘fashion show’ where girls and staff display the cultural dress of their heritage. People discuss what makes them who they are and our caterers showcase cuisine from the nations of our kitchen staff.
Black History Month
Every year we ensure that we use the opportunity of Black History Month to amplify Black voices and honour Black heritage through a series of enriching activities, workshops, and discussions. Last year’s theme was ‘Reclaiming Narratives’ and we enjoyed hearing from pupils and staff as well as external speakers. Understanding each other’s heritage and experiences enriches us as a community.
South Asian Heritage Month
At the end of the summer term, everyone is invited to wear the colours of the flags of the countries of South Asia: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Pakistan, Nepal, Sri Lanka and the Maldives, in celebration of South Asian Heritage Month. We enjoy a culturally rich assembly led by our teachers and pupils, who share their heritage, culture, and family stories with us. It is important for all of us to learn, understand, and embrace each other’s cultures so that we can continue to show support and respect for one another.
Neurodiversity Champions
At Sydenham, we value courage, character, and kindness — and respecting differences is key to upholding our school community. Neurological differences mean that some may find certain things challenging that others find easy — and vice versa. Neurodiversity is about understanding that these differences are not “abnormal,” but simply another way of thinking and being.
What will you discover?
